source_title: Evidence-based DSM ransomware recovery: preservation, RAM key recovery, copy decryption, and GitLab validation. - GitHub
source_excerpt:
NAS files renamed to .L0CK3D , with read-me3.txt appearing in folders? Preserve the scene first. Recovery may still be possible.
This repository helps you or your AI assistant stop further damage, save memory, find recovery keys and restore copies. There are successful PVE and community physical DSM cases. When no key can be found, some Btrfs files may still be recovered from old data blocks. What survives depends on your system; there is no universal key.
Do not reboot, power off, upgrade, reinstall or kill -9 the encryptor first. Its memory may still hold recovery material. Do not delete ciphertext, snapshots or the recycle bin to free space, and do not write recovered files back to the affected storage pool.
Stop encryption while preserving the process. Identify the malicious process before using sudo kill -STOP PID , replacing PID with its verified process ID. Check that every thread is T ; D means waiting for I/O, not successfully stopped. Names can change: do not suspend or kill processes in bulk based on a name alone.
Contain access and synchronization. Block NAS access to the Internet and other devices, checking both IPv4 and IPv6. Pause cloud and shared-folder synchronization to limit propagation. For remote work, first preserve a trusted console or restricted SSH connection so you retain access.
Save memory and the executable promptly. Do not wait for a full inventory or vulnerability attribution. Use independent storage with enough space; verify the mount before writing. Keep large dumps out of /tmp and the affected data volume. Choose a capture route below.
Test a few independent ciphertext copies. Look for intact copies of the same versions on computers, phones, in email or Git clones. Compare full SHA-256 digests or every byte before expanding recovery. Keep the original ciphertext throughout.
Restore service in a clean environment. Recovering data does not make the compromised NAS trustworthy. Follow recovery with rebuilding, credential replacement and remediation of the entry point.
If you are unfamiliar with SSH or processes, give this page to an administrator or AI assistant using the prompt below. Do not reboot the affected system to prepare tools.
“Never rebooted” does not mean “the key is still present”; “process exited” does not mean “all data is lost.” Community reports include successes and searches with no key found. See cases and verification limits .
The analyzed program generates encryption material for each file, protects it with a session key , and stores the protected record at the end of the file. The session key may remain in the encryptor's memory. A matching key can unlock those records and allow file recovery without obtaining the attacker's private key.
A separate route needs no key: Btrfs copy-on-write may retain data blocks from before the overwrite . If untouched parts of a file still reference those blocks, reconstruction may be possible. Actual extent mappings, snapshots and subsequent writes determine whether this works; a Btrfs or NoCOW label alone is insufficient. See crt106's explanation and our verification limits .
This repository's PVE case: a key recovered from memory restored an approximately 49 GiB GitLab weekly backup that matched its historical digest. An isolated restore recovered 80 projects .
Benjamin-zlt's physical-machine case : the author reports recovering about 84,500 files and checking a sample against known originals, using that machine's own key.
Community Btrfs tools : an alternative that reconstructs files from older blocks without a key. Verification varies between reports; file counts do not mean every file was compared byte for byte.
These tools target an analyzed sample and format. Other victims' reports have prompted physical-machine capture fixes and support for explicit session markers, but always test a few copies first. The repository also publishes one recovery candidate from our case ; there is currently no evidence that it decrypts another victim's files.
Read this repository's README and skills/dsm-ransomware-rescue/SKILL.md. Help me respond to a suspected C3RB3R / .L0CK3D incident. First establish the machine type, reboot history, encryptor state, management channel and independent destination storage. Within existing authorization, contain further damage and prioritize memory and executable preservation; do not kill a stopped encryptor. Validate candidate keys and full files on independent copies first. If no key is available, assess snapshots and Btrfs old-block recovery. Do not automatically reboot, execute malware or write to the affected volume. Clearly distinguish verified results from candidates.
Add your system version, physical/virtual setup, discovery time, reboot history and available backups. Do not publish passwords, memory dumps, keys or business files.
Evidence-based DSM ransomware recovery: preservation, RAM key recovery, copy decryption, and GitLab validation.
